about: PR 8: the words agents read. Every text below was approved by the owner on 2026-10-29 on the review page, as drafted. 'new' is the approved text exactly as a client receives it; placeholders keep their meaning. Titles go in both the tool's top-level title and annotations.title. C29 has two variants for a one-second wait and for no known wait. Items marked unchanged keep their words.

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the top-level "title" and as "annotations.title" of upload_artifact.
items.new: Upload a file

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the description of upload_artifact.
items.old: Upload a file you generated (screenshot, log, HAR, report) to Veilfile and get back a private, expiring URL to share with the user. Never upload credentials, keys or other secrets: every file is secret-scanned, and on_secret="reject" (recommended) refuses a file that trips the scanner without storing it. If the upload response contains non-empty secret_flags, do NOT share the link: ask the user whether to keep or revoke the upload first. For files larger than a few MB, use create_upload_url instead of base64.
items.new: Upload a file from base64 content and return its id, its private share link as url, expires_at, size_bytes and secret_flags. The link stops working when the file expires. The decoded file can be up to 25 MiB; for larger files, create_upload_url takes the bytes by PUT instead. The secret scan reads the first 1 MiB of the file, and secret_flags names each kind of secret-shaped content it finds. With on_secret "flag", the default, a flagged file is stored and the result adds a warning and secret_flag_locations. With on_secret "reject", a flagged file is not stored and the call returns the secret_detected error.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of upload_artifact.
items.old: File name including extension, e.g. "screenshot.png".
items.new: This is the file name, including its extension, such as screenshot.png. The allowed extensions are png, jpg, jpeg, webp, gif, txt, md, log, json, har and pdf, and the file's contents must match its extension.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of upload_artifact.
items.old: Standard base64 of the file bytes (A-Z a-z 0-9 + / with = padding). Line breaks and a "data:<mime>;base64," prefix are accepted. Decoded size must be <= 25 MiB.
items.new: This is the file's content as standard base64. Line breaks and a data:<mime>;base64, prefix are accepted. The decoded file can be up to 25 MiB.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of upload_artifact.
items.old: Ignored: the server derives the type from the file extension. Accepted for compatibility.
items.new: The server does not use this value; it takes the file's type from the extension in filename. If you send it, it must be a string.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of upload_artifact.
items.old: Optional days until the link expires. Omitting it gives the plan maximum. Values above the plan maximum are clamped down (never rejected); the result includes "ttl_adjusted": true when clamping changed your value, so always read expires_at.
items.new: This is the number of days until the link expires, as a whole number of 1 or more. If you leave it out, the link expires at the plan's maximum, which is 7 days on Free, 90 on Team and 365 on Scale. A larger value is lowered to the plan's maximum, and the result then includes ttl_adjusted: true. A value of zero or less is rejected. The result's expires_at is the applied expiry.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of upload_artifact.
items.old: Optional. "reject" (recommended) rejects the upload with an error when any secret flag fires (nothing is stored); default "flag" stores the file and reports the flags with a warning.
items.new: The value is either "flag" or "reject", and the default is "flag". With "flag", a file with secret-shaped content is stored, and the result lists secret_flags and adds a warning and secret_flag_locations. With "reject", that file is not stored and the call returns the secret_detected error.

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the top-level "title" and as "annotations.title" of create_upload_url.
items.new: Create an upload URL

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the description of create_upload_url.
items.old: Mint a one-time upload URL for a file too large to pass through the model as base64 (screenshots, HAR files, log bundles). PUT the raw file bytes to the returned upload_url from your shell within 15 minutes (e.g. curl --upload-file). The server runs the full upload pipeline on the bytes — type verification, secret scan, storage — and answers 201 with the artifact. The URL is single-use and needs no API key: the token is the auth.
items.new: Create a one-time upload URL for a file too large to send as base64 through upload_artifact. The result has upload_url, expires_at, max_size_bytes (25 MiB), ttl_days and filename. The URL is valid for 15 minutes and needs no API key. A PUT of the file's raw bytes to it, for example with curl --upload-file, runs the same type check and secret scan as upload_artifact and answers 201 with the same fields that upload_artifact returns. The first successful PUT uses up the URL. A PUT that fails can be retried until the URL expires, except one blocked as content_not_allowed. The URL also stops working if the API key that created it is revoked or the connected app that created it is disconnected.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of create_upload_url.
items.old: File name including extension, e.g. "screenshot.png".
items.new: This is the file name, including its extension, such as screenshot.png. The extension is checked when the URL is created, and the allowed extensions are png, jpg, jpeg, webp, gif, txt, md, log, json, har and pdf.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of create_upload_url.
items.old: Optional days until the link expires. Omitting it gives the plan maximum; above-max values are clamped down. The result reports the applied ttl_days and "ttl_adjusted": true when clamping changed your value.
items.new: This is the number of days until the link expires, as a whole number of 1 or more. If you leave it out, the link expires at the plan's maximum, which is 7 days on Free, 90 on Team and 365 on Scale. A larger value is lowered to the plan's maximum, and the result then includes ttl_adjusted: true. A value of zero or less is rejected. The days count from the PUT, and the result's ttl_days is the applied value.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of create_upload_url.
items.old: Optional "reject" to reject the PUT when any secret flag fires.
items.new: The value is either "flag" or "reject", and the default is "flag". With "reject", a PUT of a flagged file fails with the secret_detected error, the file is not stored and the URL stays usable until it expires. With "flag", a flagged file is stored and the result lists its secret_flags and adds a warning and secret_flag_locations.

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the top-level "title" and as "annotations.title" of list_artifacts.
items.new: List files

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the description of list_artifacts.
items.old: List this workspace's artifacts, newest first.
items.new: List the files in this workspace, newest first. Each entry has id, filename, mime_type, size_bytes, url, expires_at, secret_flags and created_at. Expired files that are not yet deleted are included. The tool changes nothing.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of list_artifacts.
items.old: Maximum artifacts to return.
items.new: This is the maximum number of files to return. The range is 1 to 200, the default is 50, and a value outside the range is moved to the nearest end of it. Files beyond the limit are not returned, and there is no paging.

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the top-level "title" and as "annotations.title" of revoke_artifact.
items.new: Revoke a file

items.trigger: A client reads this in tools/list as the description of revoke_artifact.
items.old: Revoke (delete) an artifact immediately by its id. The URL stops working at once.
items.new: Revoke a file by its id. Its link stops working at once and the file is deleted. The result is revoked: true, or revoked: false when this workspace has no file with that id. If storage could not be reached, the result adds storage_deleted: false and a later sweep finishes the deletion. Repeating the call is harmless.

items.trigger: A client reads this in the inputSchema of revoke_artifact.
items.old: Artifact id (uuid) as returned by upload_artifact.
items.new: This is the id of the file to revoke, a UUID. Both upload_artifact and list_artifacts return it.

items.old: Method "{method}" not allowed.
items.new: The method {method} is not allowed for this URL. The Allow response header lists the methods it accepts.

items.trigger: A request whose Content-Type no parser accepts gets this as "error" (HTTP 415).
items.old: Unsupported media type "{media_type}" in request.
items.new: The content type "{media_type}" is not accepted here. Set the Content-Type header to one the endpoint accepts, such as application/json.

items.trigger: A request whose Accept header no renderer can satisfy gets this as "error" (HTTP 406).
items.old: Could not satisfy the request Accept header.
items.new: The API cannot send a response in the format the Accept header asks for. Ask for application/json, or leave the header out.

items.trigger: A GET /a/<token> while storage is down returns this as a text/plain body.
items.old: This file is temporarily unavailable. Try again in about 30 seconds.
items.new: This file is temporarily unavailable. Try again in about 30 seconds.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/keys whose "name" is present and not a string (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: name must be a string.
items.new: The name must be a string. Send name as text, or leave it out.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/keys with a name longer than the field allows (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: name must be at most {max_length} characters.
items.new: The name is longer than {max_length} characters. Use a shorter name.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/keys whose name has control characters (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: name must not contain control characters.
items.new: The name contains control characters. Remove them and try again.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/keys whose JSON body is not an object (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: Request body must be a JSON object.
items.new: The request body must be a JSON object. Send the body as an object, such as one with a name field.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/keys when the workspace has its plan's number of active keys (HTTP 402) gets this as "error".
items.old: API key limit for your plan has been reached.
items.new: Your workspace has reached its plan's API key limit. Revoke a key or upgrade your plan.

items.trigger: A DELETE /api/v1/keys/<id> for a key that is not in the caller's workspace, or does not exist (HTTP 404), gets this as "error".
items.old: No APIKey matches the given query.
items.new: No API key with that id exists in this workspace. Check the id.

items.trigger: A DELETE /api/v1/keys/<id> by an API key naming a different key (HTTP 403) gets this as "error".
items.old: An API key can only revoke itself. Revoke other keys from the dashboard.
items.new: An API key can only revoke itself. Revoke other keys from the dashboard.

items.trigger: A GET /api/v1/artifacts with a bad limit or cursor (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: limit must be an integer and cursor a value from X-Next-Cursor.
items.new: The limit must be a whole number, and the cursor must be a value from the X-Next-Cursor header. Correct the one that is wrong, or leave both out.

items.trigger: A DELETE /api/v1/artifacts/<id> for a file that is not in the caller's workspace, or does not exist (HTTP 404), gets this as "error".
items.old: Artifact not found.
items.new: No file with that id exists in this workspace. Check the id.

items.trigger: A DELETE /api/v1/oauth/grants/<app_id> for an app that is not connected, or not the caller's (HTTP 404), gets this as "error".
items.old: Connected app not found.
items.new: No connected app with that id exists for you. Check the id under Connected apps on the dashboard.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/billing/switch with a plan other than team or scale (HTTP 400) gets this as "error".
items.old: Choose the team or scale plan.
items.new: Choose the team or scale plan.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/billing/switch for a workspace with no Stripe customer, no live subscription, or no plan item (HTTP 409) gets this as "error".
items.old: This workspace has no active subscription to change. Use checkout to subscribe.
items.new: This workspace has no active subscription to change. Subscribe first with POST /api/v1/billing/checkout.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/billing/switch for a workspace with several entitled subscriptions (HTTP 409) gets this as "error".
items.old: This workspace has more than one subscription. Use Manage billing to cancel the extra one, or contact support.
items.new: This workspace has more than one subscription. Use Manage billing to cancel the extra one, or contact support.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/billing/switch while the subscription is past due (HTTP 409) gets this as "error".
items.old: Your last payment failed. Update your payment method under Manage billing before changing plans.
items.new: Your last payment failed. Update your payment method under Manage billing before changing plans.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/billing/switch whose plan-change payment did not go through, when Stripe gave an invoice page (HTTP 402), gets this as "error"; the body also has "plan" and "invoice_url".
items.old: The payment for the plan change did not go through, so your plan is unchanged. Complete the payment on the invoice page (your bank may ask you to confirm it), or update your payment method under Manage billing and switch again.
items.new: The payment for the plan change did not go through, so your plan is unchanged. Complete the payment on the invoice page (your bank may ask you to confirm it), or update your payment method under Manage billing and switch again.

items.trigger: The same refusal when Stripe gave no invoice page (HTTP 402) gets this as "error"; "invoice_url" is null.
items.old: The payment for the plan change did not go through, so your plan is unchanged. Update your payment method under Manage billing, then switch again.
items.new: The payment for the plan change did not go through, so your plan is unchanged. Update your payment method under Manage billing, then switch again.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/device/code over the per-IP hourly limit (HTTP 429, Retry-After header) gets this as "error".
items.old: Too many device code requests. Try again later.
items.new: Too many sign-ins were started from this network in the past hour. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then run veilfile login again.

items.trigger: A POST /api/v1/device/code while too many device sign-ins are pending site-wide (HTTP 429, Retry-After: 60) gets this as "error".
items.old: Too many sign-ins in progress. Try again in a minute.
items.new: Too many sign-ins are in progress. Run veilfile login again in a minute.

items.trigger: A poll of POST /api/v1/device/token after the approving account was deactivated (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description", with "error": "access_denied".
items.old: The account that approved this login is no longer active.
items.new: The account that approved this login is no longer active. Run veilfile login again and approve it from an active account.

items.trigger: A poll of POST /api/v1/device/token when the plan's key limit was reached after approval (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description", with "error": "access_denied".
items.old: Your plan's API key limit has been reached. Run veilfile login again and choose a key to replace, or revoke one in the dashboard.
items.new: Your workspace has reached its plan's API key limit. Run veilfile login again and choose a key to replace, or revoke a key in the dashboard.

items.trigger: A request to /o/register/, /o/token/ or /o/revoke_token/ over the per-IP hourly limit (HTTP 429, Retry-After header) gets this as "error_description", with "error": "rate_limited".
items.old: Too many requests. Try again later.
items.new: Too many requests came from this network in the past hour. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header, then try again.

items.trigger: A dynamic client registration (POST or PUT /o/register/) whose body is over 16 KiB (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Client metadata must be 16 KiB or smaller.
items.new: The request body is larger than 16 KiB. Send client metadata of 16 KiB or less.

items.trigger: A dynamic client registration whose JSON is nested too deeply to parse (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Request body must be valid JSON
items.new: The request body is nested too deeply to read as JSON. Send JSON with fewer levels of nesting.

items.trigger: A dynamic client registration with a NUL character or an unpaired surrogate anywhere in the body (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Client metadata must not contain NUL characters or unpaired surrogates.
items.new: The client metadata contains a NUL character or an unpaired surrogate. Remove it and register again.

items.trigger: A dynamic client registration whose grant_types names anything other than authorization_code or refresh_token (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Unsupported grant_type {grant_type[:80]!r}: Veilfile clients use authorization_code (with refresh_token).
items.new: The grant_type {grant_type[:80]!r} is not supported. Use authorization_code, refresh_token or both.

items.trigger: A dynamic client registration with a redirect_uri that fails any of D11 to D25 (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Rejected redirect_uri {shown!r}: {reason}
items.new: The redirect_uri {shown!r} was rejected. {reason}

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description, after "Rejected redirect_uri ...:". Cause: the redirect_uri is missing, empty or not a string.
items.old: redirect_uri must be a non-empty string
items.new: The redirect_uri must be a non-empty string.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri is longer than 2048 characters (_MAX_REDIRECT_URI_LENGTH, oauth.py:377).
items.old: redirect_uri is too long
items.new: The redirect_uri must be 2048 characters or fewer.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri contains a non-ASCII character.
items.old: redirect_uri must be ASCII
items.new: The redirect_uri must use ASCII characters only.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri contains a character below 32 or 127.
items.old: redirect_uri must not contain control characters
items.new: The redirect_uri must not contain control characters.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri contains a space or other whitespace.
items.old: redirect_uri must not contain whitespace
items.new: The redirect_uri must not contain spaces or other whitespace.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: urlsplit raised ValueError.
items.old: redirect_uri is malformed
items.new: The redirect_uri could not be parsed as a URI. Send a well-formed URI.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri has any scheme other than http or https (a native app's custom scheme, for example).
items.old: redirect_uri must use the http or https scheme
items.new: The redirect_uri must use the http or https scheme.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri contains user:password@ in the host part.
items.old: redirect_uri must not include userinfo
items.new: The redirect_uri must not include a username or password.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: there is no host after the scheme.
items.old: redirect_uri must include a host
items.new: The redirect_uri must include a host.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the redirect_uri contains a fragment (#).
items.old: redirect_uri must not include a fragment
items.new: The redirect_uri must not include a fragment, the part after #.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the host is a private, reserved, link-local, multicast or unspecified IP address (oauth.py:435-445).
items.old: redirect_uri must not target a private, reserved, or link-local address
items.new: The redirect_uri host must not be a private, reserved, link-local, multicast or unspecified IP address.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the host is localhost, .localhost, .local or a name with no dot (oauth.py:451-461).
items.old: redirect_uri must use a public DNS name (localhost and local names are not allowed; native apps use a literal loopback IP)
items.new: The redirect_uri host must be a public DNS name, not localhost, a .localhost name, a .local name or a name without a dot. A native app uses a literal loopback IP address instead.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the host's last label looks like a number, such as 127.1 (oauth.py:462-470).
items.old: redirect_uri host must be a DNS name or a dotted-quad or bracketed IPv6 literal
items.new: The redirect_uri host must be a DNS name or a full IP address, with IPv4 written as four numbers separated by dots and IPv6 in brackets.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: the host is over 253 characters or has an invalid label (oauth.py:471-474).
items.old: redirect_uri host is malformed
items.new: The redirect_uri host is not a valid DNS name. Use at most 253 characters in total, with labels separated by single dots, each label 1 to 63 characters of letters, digits and hyphens, and no label starting or ending with a hyphen.

items.trigger: Part of D10's error_description. Cause: http to a host that is not a literal loopback IP address (oauth.py:475-479).
items.old: redirect_uri must use https (http is only allowed for literal loopback IP redirect URIs, RFC 8252)
items.new: The redirect_uri must use https, except for a literal loopback IP address such as 127.0.0.1 or [::1].

items.trigger: A POST /o/token/ with a grant_type other than authorization_code or refresh_token (HTTP 400) gets this as "error_description".
items.old: Only the authorization_code and refresh_token grants are supported.
items.new: The grant_type is not supported. Use authorization_code or refresh_token.

items.kind: new paragraph after step 4 of "Releasing the CLIs"
items.new: npm and PyPI each trust one publisher, release.yml in this repository. npm 0.4.1 was the first release from here, and PyPI's next release will be its first. Only the maintainers team can create npm-v* and pypi-v* tags (the release-tags ruleset), so Muse's account pushes them after the owner's go-ahead.

items.new: Every published CLI (npm `veilfile` 0.2.0, 0.4.0 and 0.4.1, PyPI `veilfile` 0.3.0 and 0.4.0)
